political savagery of literary journalism at that time. The absence of any reference to Keats’s
death by either S. or Mary in the days immediately following the arrival of Smith’s letter is
doubtless explained by their preoccupation with the immediate money problem to which
they were alerted in that letter. Mary wrote to Leigh Hunt on 17 April confirming that
‘[w]e have been much shocked to hear of Keats’ death — and sorry that it was in no way
permitted us to be of any use to him since his arrival in Italy’ (there is a suggestion here
that the antipathy towards S. of members of Keats’s circle may have prompted them to dis-
courage him from accepting S.’s invitation), and she wrote two days later to inform Maria
Gisborne of the news (Mary L i 189, 197). It is unlikely that S. made any sustained effort
of composition prompted by Keats’s death in the weeks immediately following receipt of
